Hi I always have problems in making bright white light reflection copies, but don't really understand what's my problem. 

I think beam ratio is one of the crucial factors. I don't think my problem is movement, but I am not sure. I have no stability problems in transmission and rainbow setups. In white light copies the image often is complete there , but dim. Is there a possibility to check the stability of the setup? Can I make the fringes visible to see movement? I don't mean a Michelson interferometer, as this doesn't take the setup in to account. How do you check stability?

Concerning ratio:

In Saxby's Practical Holography (3rd edition) page 51 is an explanation about ratios. Here it reads that object beam intensity is 3 times higher than reference beam? Is that right? Anyway, explaining box 4.2 is missing in the book?

What is the convention for ratios ? If there is 3:1, is it obj:ref or ref:obj ? 

Page 177 says it vice versa???

How do you adjust ratio for your WLR copies?

Any help or explanation would be good.

posts.author: jsfisher
posts.content_md:
Yes, Box 4.2 appears to be missing, but I think you are misinterpreting what was written on page 51.

> The ideal beam intensity ratio (see Box 4.2) for a reflection hologram is low, somewhere between 1.5 :1 and 3 : 1. This means that the intensity of the object beam needs to be as high as possible, and with subject matter that is deep or not very bright it is difficult to achieve the optimum ratio. To obtain bright reflection holograms of deep or dark objects you need to illuminate the subject independently, and to control the beam intensity ratio (Fig. 4.6).

A beam ratio of 3:1, for example, is reference being 3 times brighter than object beam. In figure 4.6, a neutral density filter is in place to lower the brightness of the reference beam, bringing the ratio down from maybe 10:1 to a more reasonable 3:1
